description:
Where a satellite is now, or at a given time: the point on Earth straight below it (latDeg, lonDeg), its altitude (altitudeKm), and whether it is sunlit, with url (its page on seeksat.com). For every satellite in the sky right now use find_satellites_up_now; for when it passes over use find_passes or find_next_visible_pass; for its orbit and TLE use get_satellite.

With a place (lat and lon, or location), it also gives where the satellite is in that place's sky: azimuthDeg (degrees clockwise from north), elevationDeg (apparent, with refraction; negative when below the horizon), rangeKm (straight-line distance) and aboveHorizon. The place also sets the time zone for local times and for reading a time with no offset; without one, times are UTC.

With durationMinutes, it also gives the ground track from that time on: track, one point every stepSeconds (up to a day, at most 720 points), each with time, latDeg, lonDeg, altitudeKm and sunlit, plus the four sky fields when a place is given (a pointing table), and trackStepSeconds, the step used. lonDeg jumps between 180 and -180 where the track crosses the antimeridian, so split a drawn line there.

A time more than 30 days from the orbital elements' epoch is refused.

durationMinutes.description: how long a ground track to return, in minutes from time, up to 1440 (a day); about 93 is one ISS orbit. Omit for one position.

lat.description: observer latitude in decimal degrees, north positive (-90 to 90). Give it with lon, or give location instead.

location.description: where the observer is, when lat and lon are not given (they win when both are): a Maidenhead grid square (EN52, EN52ve, EN52ve12), coordinates in any common form ("41.88, -87.63", "41.88N 87.63W", "41°52'48"N 87°37'48"W", a Google Maps link or geo: URI), all read locally, or a place name (city, address, landmark) looked up with OpenStreetMap. Prefer lat and lon, or a grid square, when you have them: a place name is a network lookup. Optional here: with it, the result adds azimuth and elevation from there.

lon.description: observer longitude in decimal degrees, east positive and west negative (-180 to 180).

passTime.description: old name for time; still accepted.

satellite.description: NORAD catalog number (as a number or a string) or a name, e.g. 25544, "25544" or "iss".

stepSeconds.description: seconds between track points, 10 to 3600. Default 60, or wider when needed to keep the track to 720 points; a step you give that would make more is refused, naming the smallest that fits.

time.description: when (with durationMinutes, where the track starts). Default: now. ISO 8601 with Z or an offset, e.g. "2026-11-14T21:00:00-06:00"; a time with no offset, e.g. "2026-11-14T21:00", is read in the observer's time zone, and the result echoes how it was read (interpretedAs). A local time the clocks skip at a daylight-saving change is moved forward, with a note.

name: get_position
title: Satellite position
